title: Susan Smith, Who Drowned Her 2 Young Sons 32 Years Ago, Makes Another Bid for Freedom as Boys’ Dad Fights Release

 David Smith plans to oppose his ex-wife’s release as she faces a parole board for the second time
 Nicole Acosta Mon, 16 November 2026 at 10:05 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. David Smith in 1995; Susan Smith in a July 2026 mugshot.
Credit: Ruth Fremson/AP; SC Dept of Corrections NEED TO KNOW
 David Smith is speaking out against the potential release of his ex-wife, Susan Smith, who was convicted of murdering their two sons in 1994
 Susan has become eligible for parole for a second time and will face the parole board this week
 "If I have a choice, I'd want her to stay in prison until she dies," David told CNN in a report published on Sunday, Nov. 15
 Days before convicted murderer Susan Smith faces a South Carolina parole board for the second time, her ex-husband is speaking out against her potential release.
 Susan, now 55, was sentenced to life in prison for drowning her two sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alex, in 1994 after falsely claiming a Black man carjacked her at a stop light with her children still inside.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement She became eligible for parole in November 2024 after serving 30 years of her murder sentence, but that request was ultimately denied . Susan was required to wait two years before being considered for release again; her second parole hearing is scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 19.
 Her ex-husband and father of the boys, David Smith, has been open about his feelings towards Susan and opposed her release two years ago.
 "God gives us free choice, and she made free choice that night to end their lives," David said of Susan at the parole hearing in 2024, per CNN. "This wasn't a tragic mistake. She purposely meant to end their lives. I never have felt any remorse from her. She never expressed any to me."
 In a new report published by CNN on Sunday, Nov. 15, David, now 56, made clear that his position has not changed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It's been hard, hard," he told the news outlet exclusively. "If I have a choice, I'd want her to stay in prison until she dies."
 Susan Smith in 1995. 
 Credit: Brooks Kraft LLC/Sygma via Getty 
 David also said he hopes members of the parole board will consider the case from his perspective. "It's important for me to remind the parole board that it may be 32 years, but for me it's still like yesterday. 32 years hasn't changed the heartache," the outlet reported.
 In the nine days after then-23-year-old Susan reported the apparent carjacking to police, she made emotional pleas on national television for her children to be returned home safely. But as her story began to unravel, she admitted that there was no carjacker and that she had let her car roll into a lake with her children still strapped into their car seats.
 The story became international news and was featured on the cover of PEOPLE .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement During her murder trial, prosecutors argued that she had been having an affair with a married man who did not want children, and that after the two split she killed the boys to try and win him back. Her defense claimed she suffered postpartum depression and had a history of mental health struggles.
 "I didn't know what was going on," David told CNN. "I had believed her. I found out she killed our children on live TV."
 David has since remarried and welcomed two more children, who are now adults, but said his memories of his young sons have begun to fade.
 "People ask me, 'How old would they be today?' I don't know. I can't process that, because to me, they'll always be 3 [years] and 14 months," he said, per the outlet.
 David Smith holds up a photo of his late sons, Michael and Alex, in 1995 outside the Union County Courthouse in South Carolina. 
 Credit: Ruth Fremson/AP

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Before the parole board rejected her release in a unanimous vote two years ago, Susan told them, "I know that what I did was horrible," CNN previously reported. "I am a Christian and God is a big part of my life and I know he has forgiven me and I know that is by his grace and mercy … And I just ask that you show that same kind of mercy as well."
 Susan is currently incarcerated at the Leath Correctional Institution in Greenwood, S.C. She has earned no education credits during her time behind bars and has had a series of disciplinary infractions .
